Thanks Stacie — and thanks for attaching the SOC2 report. A few concrete items to help your security/legal review; I'll send the fillable vendor questionnaire as an attachment in this thread (partial answers included).

Summary of Redwood's typical retention/deletion posture (configurable per-customer):
- Customer data (model inputs/outputs): default retention 30 days; enterprise options: configurable to 90 days or 365 days upon contract. For Private deployments, customers can set retention to 0 (no retention) if required.
- KV/cache / request context: ephemeral caches are purged within 48 hours by default (configurable).
- Audit logs (control-plane events, auth logs): retained 365 days by default for enterprise customers; 90 days for standard hosted tiers.
- Backups / snapshots: retained 90 days by default; backups are immutable for the retention window and are only purged per policy or on explicit deletion request.
- Deletion SLA: visible deletion from active stores: typically within 48 hours; purge from backups/archive windows: up to 30 days from request to complete (we can negotiate shorter windows in contract).
- E-discovery / export: standard export job turnaround ~72 hours for scoped data pulls; expedited requests possible with SLA addendum.

Attachments: "Redwood_Vendor_Questionnaire_Partial.xlsx" (fillable). I filled in obvious fields and flagged items for your security team.

Next steps proposed:
- Redwood to send completed vendor questionnaire to security@medpulse.com by EOD Aug 4 (attached).
- Please confirm SOC2 receipt and whether a redaction is required.
- Confirm a time on Aug 11 for a 45-min security/engineering session — Rafael and Dylan will join.

If MedPulse has non-negotiable retention windows (e.g., <30 days or a legal hold process that requires immediate deletion), flag those and we'll map contract and engineering options.

Quick technical clarifications from the platform/security side:
- Encryption: all customer data at rest encrypted with customer-managed keys (KMS integration available for Dedicated/Private); backups are encrypted at rest and in transit.
- Backups: immutable snapshots retained for the configured retention window (default 90 days). Snapshots are tagged and can be purged on request — full purge from immutable backup store may require a short processing window (typically <= 30 days).
- Logs: two classes — (1) audit/control-plane logs (retained 365 days by default for enterprise), (2) request-level traces (token-level traces) retained 30 days by default; both are encrypted and can be exported via secure S3 export.
- Deletion/e-discovery: when MedPulse requests data deletion or an export, Redwood initiates deletion from active stores within 48 hours and provides an export package (if requested) within 72 hours. For legal holds, we can implement preservation flags; retrieval for e-discovery typically completes in <=72 hours but can be expedited with a paid SLA.

Happy to walk through specifics on Aug 11 — I will prepare a short one-pager on retention windows + contractual SLA options.
